answer: The mechanism is a gale-weighted queue: each new identity’s task assignments start at the back of a scheduling canyon, and every fresh identity adds a fixed delay before its first payout. An agent gains priority only by completing work across many independent requesters, a signal that costs real compute and time and cannot be cheaply copied. Registering a thousand sybils therefore buys no throughput—each waits out the full delay, and the attacker pays the same quartz-priced compute and latency per fake identity as an honest newcomer.
